name: suiteworld-2026
label: SuiteWorld 2026 — NetSuite Community
description: Targets two buyer segments within the NetSuite ecosystem ahead of SuiteWorld 2026 (Oct 25–28, Las Vegas). Segment A: decision-makers at NetSuite SIs, Oracle VARs, and SuiteCommerce agencies — pitch AOTT as a delivery arm for Shopify and SuiteCommerce builds. Segment B: IT Directors, VP Operations, and eCommerce leads at companies that run NetSuite — pitch AOTT as a direct build partner for SuiteCommerce or Shopify projects.
_note: This criteria has two buyer segments. Segment A (partner/SI): companies whose business is implementing or delivering NetSuite, Oracle, or eCommerce solutions for clients — the AOTT pitch is delivery capacity and a wider offer without growing headcount. Segment B (end-user brand): companies that run NetSuite as their ERP and need SuiteCommerce or Shopify built, customized, or integrated — the AOTT pitch is expert build execution so their team doesn't have to do it. The classifier and composer must detect the segment from the lead's headline and company before writing any message. Key detection: if the company name or headline contains implementation/SI/partner/consulting/agency signals → Segment A. If the company is a retailer, manufacturer, distributor, or brand → Segment B. When ambiguous, default to Segment A.
_classifier_note: Score both segments by the same weights, but interpret seniority signals differently. For Segment A: the buyer is a practice-owner or delivery leader (CEO, MD, VP Delivery, Director of PS, VP Partnerships). For Segment B: the buyer is an operations or technology owner (IT Director, CIO, VP Operations, Head of eCommerce, Director of Digital). Anti-patterns apply to both segments equally. Do NOT penalise Segment B leads for being at an end-user company — that is the correct target, not a negative signal. Penalise heavily for: individual technical contributors (developer, admin, engineer), pure marketing/sales roles with no build authority, and recruiter/staffing roles. The SuiteWorld context means attendees are self-selected as senior practitioners — score seniority signals more generously than in other criteria.
